messages:
maya: heads up — after the routing-policy rollout at 09:10, console charts are snappier on CANARY but main dashboard shows large TTFB and long tasks on main thread. heatmap/line charts particularly bad.
liam: can you paste the telemetry link or a quick histogram?
maya: https://telemetry.internal/reports/2419 — spike in request queues + main-thread long tasks, here's a trimmed log:
```json
{
  "route": "/v1/metrics/heatmap",
  "queue_ms_p50": 310,
  "queue_ms_p95": 1420,
  "client_side_long_tasks": 27
}
```
sanjay: looks like the new per-route throttling + small-batch fallback is creating backpressure. frontend keeps retrying prefetched tiles which bloats main thread parse/hydration.
zoe: worth checking chunk load timing — we pushed microbundle-splitter last week, maybe chunk fetches are now serialized behind the route throttle.
andre: deploy-bot says routing-config canary flipped a tweak at 09:09, see message below. probably correlated.
deploy-bot: canary deploy 2026-03-20T09:09:12Z — routing-policy v2.3.1 applied to canary region.
kevin: can we temporarily widen the concurrency window for the affected route (heatmap/line) to see if it's the throttle or something else?
maya: on it. increasing concurrency to 12 for /v1/metrics/* in canary now. if perf recovers we can either tweak quota or change retry/backoff.
liam: another mitigation — add small client-side debounce during initial hydration for sparkline/heatmap tiles. reduces burst fan-out.
zoe: i'll run a flame on canary once change is live. expecting to see queue->parse stall reduce.
andre: if that buys us time we should rollback the routing tweak for prod and do a staged rollout with A/B for different quota strategies.
kevin: also consider caching identical prefix queries at the edge for 1s TTL — most of these requests are identical during nav. cheap win.
maya: quick check — enabling concurrency fixed p50 queue from 310 -> 35ms on canary. p95 down to ~210. main thread long tasks dropped 70%.
sanjay: confirms hypothesis. rough plan: 1) revert canary config to previous in prod rollout 2) implement client debounce + short edge cache 3) explore token-based quota vs per-route for heatmap endpoints 4) add telemetry to monitor queue_ms per route.
liam: I'll open a tiny PR for client debounce (30–60ms) and add a telemetry event for when tile fetches are deduped.
zoe: i'll attach flame + waterfall in the PR for the curious.
andre: i'll coordinate rollback and schedule a slower rollout with canary percentage steps.
maya: thanks all — marking this high priority for the morning. :thumbsup:
kevin: :thumbsup:
liam: noted, PR incoming.
deploy-bot: rollback executed for routing-policy canary at 09:28 — 2026-03-20T09:28:40Z
maya: monitoring prod now, will post if anything else pops up.
